advisor.commerce.caveats: Trade routes are not built: no open freight flows between states were found (DOSM's trade tables are national external trade). Military bases are not built either: no open list of properties was found to check them against.

Roads and rail are Natural Earth's 1:10m lines, map art rather than a survey: many Sabah and Sarawak roads and part of the rail network are missing. Ports are not shown: there are no open cargo statistics by port, and Natural Earth's port points leave out Port Klang and Tanjung Pelepas.

Airports are those with 900,000 or more passengers in 2019, the last year before the pandemic, from Wikidata's statements; airports with no 2019 figure there (Ipoh, Kuantan, Labuan and others) are not shown. Boardings are half the total passengers, an estimate.
advisor.culture.caveats: Wonders are chosen by published rules and never by community or faith: UNESCO's World Heritage list, a short hand-picked list of parks and landmarks that are not places of worship, and the five designated Research Universities ranked by lecturers in 2025 (public universities only; at most two per city, so a third Klang Valley university is left out).

Flood figures are DOSM's estimated value of losses per year in current ringgit, from its Impact of Floods reports for 2021 to 2025, not a count of events: each year comes from the latest report that carries it, a blank is a figure DOSM did not publish, and the December 2021 floods dominate the series. For 2021 the state rows leave out agriculture and infrastructure (published for the nation only), so the state totals add up from 2022. Malaysia has no open disaster database of events, deaths or other hazards, so only floods are shown.
advisor.explorer.caveats: Population is DOSM's {year} mid-year estimate by administrative district. Six districts created in 2025 (Membakut in Sabah; Gedong, Lingga, Pantu, Sebuyau and Siburan in Sarawak) are counted in the districts they were carved from, so every figure sits on the 160 districts the map draws.

Cities are the conurbations of several whole districts (Greater Kuala Lumpur, George Town, Johor Bahru, Kuching, Kota Kinabalu; see the Almanac) and every other district of 150,000 or more residents, named after its largest town.
almanac.resources_intro: Resource markers show power plants of 25 MW or more as the World Resources Institute listed them (database v1.3.0, no capacity year recorded), named oil, gas and LNG sites that Wikidata places in Malaysia, the districts with 20,000+ ha of oil palm (Descals et al., 2019), and where durian, coconut, pineapple or sago cover at least 800–1,500 ha (DOSM, 2024). Oil and gas fields at sea are shown on the nearest coast hex. Not on the map: mines (open data gives output by state, not positions), and rubber and paddy (no district figures in open data). Press R to show or hide them.
advisor.energy.caveats: Power plants are those of 25 MW or more in WRI's Global Power Plant Database v1.3.0, which records no capacity year for Malaysian plants: plants built or closed since are not reflected, and Sarawak's large hydro stations (Bakun, Murum) are missing from it.
Some stations may be listed twice in the database (Tanjung Bin appears as two coal rows at one site; Kapar's coal and its gas row are the same company), so a state's mapped capacity can overstate it.
Oil, gas and LNG sites are the few Wikidata lists with coordinates: most Petronas fields are not on the map, and no output figures are available.
Mines are not mapped: the mineral extraction table (DOSM, from the Minerals and Geoscience Department) gives output by state, with no positions.
advisor.land.caveats: Land cover is the Sentinel-2 10 m map sampled at 7 points per hex, so small features blur into their surroundings.

That map classes plantations as trees. Oil palm is moved to cropland using the Descals et al. 2019 map (10 m; a sample point on a 1 km block that is at least half oil palm), but rubber and other tree crops, and oil palm planted since 2019, still read as forest, so tree cover is still overstated, most in Johor, Perak, Kedah and Kelantan.
Forest reserve area is the state's gazetted permanent reserved forest (Forestry Department): it is not a land-cover share.
advisor.economy.gdp_note: Value added by each sector in constant 2015 ringgit, where the work is done (the states summed, with offshore oil and gas in mining). Hover a sector to light up the states where it is the biggest share of the economy.
advisor.economy.workers_note: Employed persons by industry, counted where they live (Labour Force Survey 2021, by state). Hover an industry to light up the states where it is the biggest share of jobs; click it to rank the cities that specialise in it. City figures are estimates (see the notes below).
advisor.economy.caveats: GDP is in constant 2015 ringgit, so years compare. States and Malaysia are {year}; districts and cities are 2020, the latest year DOSM publishes by district. Offshore oil and gas belongs to no state: it is in Malaysia's GDP only, so the states add to less than the national figure.
GDP by sector has five sectors (agriculture; mining & quarrying; manufacturing; construction; services). Their shares are of GDP before import duties, so they add to a little less than GDP.
Kuala Lumpur's 2020 district GDP includes Putrajaya's (DOSM could not separate them); Putrajaya shows no district GDP.

Workers by industry are Labour Force Survey estimates by state for 2021, benchmarked to the 2020 Census. DOSM publishes no district split, so district and city figures share each state's workers by the district's 2020 GDP in the matching sector: they are estimates.
advisor.prosperity.caveats: Incomes are gross monthly household income in ringgit (HIES {census_vintage}), not annual. Poverty is the absolute poverty rate: the share of households below the national poverty line income.

Districts made of several survey districts (the parents of the districts created in 2025) and cities made of several districts use population-weighted means; their medians are the weighted mean of the medians (an approximation) and they have no Gini.
Unemployment: {unemployment_vintage}. Perlis, Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya, each one district, show their state's survey.
advisor.prosperity.poverty_note: Districts by the share of households below the national poverty line income (HIES 2024, absolute poverty). Hover a bar to outline those districts; the table lists them all.
advisor.prosperity.unemployment_note: Unemployed ÷ labour force ({unemployment_vintage}). Cities of {min}+ people.
fields.gdp: GDP in constant 2015 ringgit, counted where the work is done: {year} for states, {metro_year} for districts and cities.
fields.gdp_pc: GDP ÷ residents of the same year ({year} for states, {metro_year} for districts and cities), constant 2015 ringgit.
report.unemployment.description: Unemployed ÷ labour force, the Labour Force Survey's annual average for 2024. Malaysia is the sum of the 16 states.
report.gdp_years_hint: {regions}: {year} GDP. Cities: {metro_year}, the latest year DOSM publishes by district. All in constant 2015 ringgit.
report.gdp_per_person_hint.metros: Cities: {metro_year} GDP ÷ {metro_year} residents; cities of {min}+ people.
report.gdp_industry_credit: DOSM, {year} real GDP by sector (constant 2015 prices)
report.gdp_breakdown_note: {year} GDP by sector at constant 2015 prices, the 16 states plus offshore oil and gas (in mining); shares are of GDP before import duties.
panel.city_foot.gdp: Constant 2015 ringgit, {gdp_year} (the latest year DOSM publishes by district), summed over the city's districts; per person divides by the residents of {gdp_year}.
panel.city_foot.no_gdp: DOSM publishes no GDP for this area (Putrajaya's is inside Kuala Lumpur's).
panel.city_foot.unemployment_survey: {unemployment_vintage}; counts summed over the city's districts.
cv.economy_note: DOSM real GDP, {gdp_year}, constant 2015 ringgit, counted where the work is done. Per person divides by the residents of {gdp_year}.
cv.economy_note.no_gdp: DOSM publishes no GDP for this area (Putrajaya's is inside Kuala Lumpur's).
cv.workforce_note: Labour Force Survey 2021 workers by industry for each state, shared over districts by their 2020 GDP in the matching sector: an estimate, counted where people live.
cv.districts_counting: DOSM publishes workers by industry for states, not districts. The Labour Force Survey's 2021 workers by industry in each state are shared over the state's districts by their 2020 GDP in the matching sector, and counted where people live. Every city in a state therefore has that state's mix of service industries: read a district as the state's industry concentrated in this city, not as a count of the city's own workers.
cv.districts_note: {vintage}. ×N = location quotient against Malaysia: estimates, not counts. DOSM publishes no ports, aviation or defence workers, so there are no Harbor, Aerodrome or Encampment districts.
cv.no_districts: {name} has no workers-by-industry estimate, so it has no industry districts.
citizens.none: DOSM's population table has no row for {name}, so there are no citizen figures here.
citizens.row_missing: DOSM publishes no table for this below the national level that the map can read (occupation, how people get to work and where people were born are all missing), so this row is left out.
citizens.median_age: Median age, interpolated from DOSM's five-year age bands (mid-year estimate)
citizens.degree: Not shown: DOSM publishes education by state only, as no formal education, primary, secondary or tertiary.
citizens.note: {vintage}. Age: DOSM's mid-year estimate for the city's districts, in five-year bands, so children are 0-14. Education: DOSM publishes it by state only, so each city takes its state's mix of the labour force (people aged 15 and over in work or looking for it) in 2021; within a state every city has the same mix. Occupation, commute and place of birth are not published at this level. Figures are rounded (largest remainder) so each row adds up; hover or tap a figure for its share. ▲▼ (age only; the education row is a state mix) = at least 1.5× or at most 0.67× Malaysia's share. Rows are never split by ethnicity or religion.

layers.toggle.rail: Rail lines from Natural Earth, as map art (coverage of Malaysia is partial)

layers.airport_source: Total passengers in 2019 (Wikidata); boardings are half of them, an estimate. Hub classes are by passengers: large 5 million or more, medium 2 million, small 900,000.
advisor.commerce.pax_note: Passenger boardings in 2019, estimated as half of the total passengers (arrivals plus departures) that Wikidata records; no change on the year before is shown.
advisor.commerce.cargo_note: Malaysia has no open air-cargo figures by airport, so no airport is ranked by cargo.
advisor.culture.wonders_note: Hover a wonder to find it on the map; click to fly there. World Heritage Sites are UNESCO's list; parks and landmarks are hand-picked and not ranked; the research universities are the five the Ministry of Higher Education designated, ranked by lecturers.
advisor.culture.disasters_kicker: Flood losses, DOSM Impact of Floods
